subtype: Speaking up in a large lecture [Actor]
passage: The projector had died fifteen minutes into the lecture, so the professor was explaining eigenvalues on the whiteboard for three hundred students, and the back rows could barely hear. Jyoti had a question about the second example and kept it inside for forty minutes. Beside her, Sarita was doodling. “Last question,” the professor said, checking the clock. Jyoti's heart thudded. She put up her hand, the microphone was passed down the row, and her voice cracked as she asked. The professor answered. Behind her someone breathed out, “Thank God, I had the same one.” Two more students called out follow-ups. Sarita looked up from the doodle, grinning, and tapped Jyoti's notebook.

qa.q: How many students were in the lecture hall?
What was Jyoti afraid of while she kept the question inside for forty minutes?
qa.a: Jyoti seems afraid of seeming ignorant in front of a huge hall, since her heart thudded and her voice cracked when she finally asked.

qa.q: What small step could help a student who holds back questions in a big lecture?
qa.a: They could write the question down early, sit nearer the front, or ask at the first pause instead of waiting for the last question.

qa.q: What might the person behind Jyoti have felt when saying, “Thank God, I had the same one”?
qa.a: That person probably felt relieved and grateful that Jyoti asked it, since they had held the same doubt without saying it.

grounding: A college student holds back a question in a large hall for fear of seeming ignorant and finds that others had the same question.

subtype: Speaking up in a large lecture [Actor]
passage: Maria's question about the tax-slab example had been sitting in her notebook since ten o'clock. In the lecture hall for two hundred, the professor asked, “Any doubts?” and the room stayed silent, as it always did. Everyone else understands, Maria thought, and kept her hand under her thigh. After class, in the canteen, Preeti pushed a plate of samosas toward her. “You looked puzzled. What was it?” When Maria told them, three others at the table said, “That confused me too!” and one asked, “Why didn't you ask?” Maria laughed at herself. Next morning she took a seat in the second row, and when the professor asked for doubts, hers was the first hand up.

qa.q: Where did Maria talk about her question after class?
qa.a: Maria talked about it in the canteen.

qa.q: Why did Maria keep her hand under her thigh when the professor asked, “Any doubts?”
qa.a: Maria assumed that everyone else understood and feared looking ignorant if she was the only one asking.

qa.q: What changed for Maria after the canteen talk?
qa.a: Maria learned that three others had the same doubt, laughed at herself, and next morning sat in the second row and asked first.

qa.q: What might Preeti have noticed about Maria that made Preeti ask, “What was it?”
qa.a: Preeti seems to have noticed the puzzled look on Maria's face and wanted to help, which fits pushing the plate over and asking kindly.

grounding: A college student holds back a question in a big hall, then finds in the canteen that others had the same doubt, and asks the next day.
